comparison: Both evaluations strongly support the central finding that autoinhibited LRRK2 can bind and assemble on microtubules (C9, C10, C50, C51, C83, C93). OpenEval emphasizes the cryo-ET evidence resolving a key open question, while peer reviewers unanimously acknowledge this as a major discovery with no concerns raised.

Both evaluations support the novel structural finding of N-terminal repeat ordering and new interface formation (C12, C66, C67, C68, C86, C87). OpenEval provides detailed validation of focused refinement methods, while peer reviewers highlight this as a significant advance in understanding LRRK2 structure.

Perfect agreement on the geometric differences between autoinhibited and active-like assemblies (C13, C74, C75, C76, C85). Both evaluations accept the ~90° helical angle as a clearly distinct structural feature supported by quantitative analysis.

Both evaluations support the finding of shorter oligomers in autoinhibited state (C14, C78, C79, C94). OpenEval notes the consistency across conditions and characterizes the inference about stability as reasonable but needing validation, while peer reviewers accept the reduced stability interpretation more directly.

Complete agreement on conserved structural interfaces between autoinhibited and active-like states (C11, C63, C73). Both evaluations accept these shared features as important mechanistic insights without raising concerns.

Both evaluations recognize the technical achievement of highest-resolution LRRK2 filament structure via subtomogram averaging (C54, C55). Peer reviewers explicitly praise this as a major technical advance, while OpenEval notes appropriate resolution estimates.

Both evaluations support the structural similarity to prior autoinhibited structures and the finding that MLi-2 does not induce kinase closure (C57, C58, C60, C92). OpenEval provides detailed map references, while peer reviewers accept the conformational assignment despite medium resolution.

Both evaluations accept the consistency of oligomer properties across different inhibitor conditions (C80, C81, C82). OpenEval explicitly characterizes the minor GZD-824 difference, while peer reviewers implicitly accept these comparative findings without challenge.

Partial overlap on structural characterization claims (C52, C53, C62). OpenEval provides detailed structural analysis including ARM domain flexibility, while peer reviewers focus more on the core finding of autoinhibited assembly without detailed structural commentary on these specific features.
